correctness.rationale: A torsion on C(T^d) is precisely multiplication by a continuous unimodular function. A Lipschitz function has a winding vector k with norm at most its Lipschitz seminorm because the averaged phase gradient equals k. For fixed winding, the real logarithmic phase-error is continuous and has Haar mean <k,beta>-arg(lambda). If the chordal defect is less than 2, connectedness places all errors in one interval of angular width less than 2pi and the mean lies there too, giving the lower bound by the corresponding character distance; if defect equals 2, the lower bound is automatic. Characters attain the bound exactly. Equality at defect less than 2 forces an invariant real phase, constant under dense translations. This reconstructs definitions, normalization, quantifiers and boundary cases; finite numerical grids are not invoked as proof.

originality.rationale: Example 3.2 of the examined 2026 source establishes no exact torsion anticommuter for an irrational circle rotation, but does not optimize the operator-norm defect by a Lipschitz bound, treat all torus dimensions, or establish rigidity of optimizing unimodular multipliers. The full proof of the new sharp metric-constrained formula is not an implication of either spectral cyclicity or the elementary knowledge of characters. Several semantic and literal-formulation searches revealed no covering source. The residual risk of unindexed topological cohomology literature is acknowledged. Full-text comparisons with Exel (1992) and Hua–Lin (2014) identify general commutator or trace/Bott obstructions but no fixed-translation Lipschitz-constrained sharp profile or all-optimizer classification. The prior results do not directly imply the combined metric bound and rigidity.
residual_risks: The exact winding-class uniform cocycle inequality could occur in unindexed classical topological-cohomology or approximate-eigenfunction literature; keyword search alone cannot rule this out.
Several tangential related research records were compared only at title and abstract level; they were not used for a definitive full-text NOT_COVERING claim.

value.rationale: The exact, dimension-independent operator-norm/Lipschitz budget tradeoff answers a natural quantitative gap from an explicit nonexistence example in the recent theory of positive-operator cyclicity. It is a complete optimizer classification, with a nontrivial arithmetic dependence and a rigorous separation between full peripheral spectrum and attainable exact intertwining. The Lipschitz budget measures intrinsic phase complexity rather than an arbitrary finite slice; the value is this precise natural invariant, not a claimed global spectral theorem.
